name: role census
formula: T, D, S = |{h in picks : role(h) = r}| for r in {tank, damage, support}; always T+D+S = |picks|
rationale: every other shape heuristic reads these three counts; stating them first makes the rest auditable

name: tankless flag
formula: flag iff T = 0
rationale: no one makes space: the comp must win on range or flank tempo, and the dossier should say so out loud

name: triple-DPS flag
formula: flag iff D >= 3
rationale: wins the fights it starts and loses attrition; a deliberate shape, but never an accidental one

name: support drought flag
formula: flag iff S = 0
rationale: sustain becomes spawn-door only; the strongest single warning a shape can carry

name: solo-heal flag
formula: flag iff S = 1
rationale: one support is a plan only when the other four peel for them or self-sustain

name: double-tank flag
formula: flag iff T >= 2
rationale: two frontlines trade damage output for space; worth naming because open queue allows it

name: archetype deviation
formula: dev = SUM over roles r of max(0, count_r - slots_r), slots from the map's top-style comp_archetypes row
rationale: measures how far the locked picks already sit from the shape the map's own playstyle wants

name: open-slot role demand
formula: demand_r = max(0, slots_r - count_r) per role for the map archetype; lists what the open slots owe
rationale: turns deviation into a prescription: not just 'off-shape' but which roles the remaining picks should fill

name: subrole balance
formula: distinct subroles among picks / |picks|; 1.0 = every pick brings a different job
rationale: two main tanks or two flex supports overlap jobs even when the role counts look fine

name: role-flex reserve
formula: |{c in C : role(c) = argmax_r demand_r}|; how deep the pool runs for the neediest role
rationale: a demand the pool cannot fill is a different problem than one with twelve answers

name: peak kit heal
formula: peak(h) = MAX over h's ability_stats and weapon_stats of value where stat_key in (heal, hps)
rationale: the kit's own biggest heal number, ability or weapon side - measured, not judged

name: healing supply vs bench
formula: supply = SUM peak(h) over locked supports; bench = 2 x median(peak over the whole support roster)
rationale: 'enough healing' needs a denominator; the roster median is the only honest one the schema holds

name: under-healed flag
formula: flag iff S >= 2 and supply < HEAL_MARGIN x bench
rationale: only fires when the support line is complete and still light - two Zens is a choice, name it

name: self-sustain census
formula: |{h in picks : h has a heal stat targeting self}|
rationale: the schema stores heal amounts but not who receives them; needs a target column on ability_stats

name: anti-heal exposure
formula: |{e in E : e has healing_mod stat < 0}| and the worst value
rationale: a comp built on sustain answers Ana's grenade differently than one built on burst; the -100 is in the data

name: overhealth supply
formula: SUM over picks of MAX overhealth stat per kit
rationale: temporary health is burst insurance the healing-supply number does not see

name: healing amplification stack
formula: |{h in picks : h has healing_mod stat > 0}| and the product of (1 + mod)
rationale: amp multiplies the supply number; two amps on one comp is a sustain identity

name: burst-vs-drip mix
formula: per support: ability-side max heal / weapon-side max heal; >2 = burst kit, <1 = drip kit
rationale: 350 supply from burst kits and 350 from drip kits survive different damage profiles

name: sustain uptime proxy
formula: per heal ability: duration / (duration + cooldown), using each kit's own stats
rationale: peak heal on a 14s cooldown is not the same supply as peak heal every 4s

name: lifeline redundancy
formula: |{h in picks : peak(h) > 0}|; count of picks carrying any healing at all
rationale: when the count is exactly S, killing the supports ends the sustain; off-role healing is redundancy

name: frontline pool
formula: SUM over tanks of pool(h), pool = health + shield + armor
rationale: the literal hit points standing between the enemy and the backline

name: armor share
formula: armor(h) / pool(h) per tank, reported beside the pool
rationale: armor discounts sustained fire; the same pool with more armor beats spam and loses to burst less

name: team effective HP
formula: SUM pool(h) over all five picks
rationale: the ceiling on how much damage the comp absorbs before the first death, ignoring healing

name: enemy barrier audit
formula: per enemy: MAX barrier_health stat in kit; lists every barrier the enemy fields
rationale: a 750hp Brigitte shield and a 1500hp Rein wall demand different amounts of chew

name: barrier-pierce coverage
formula: {h in A union C : h has ignores_barrier stat = 1}
rationale: the direct answer to the audit: who simply does not care about the barrier

name: armor-shred need
formula: SUM armor over enemies vs |{h in picks : beam weapon or ignores_armor stat}|
rationale: heavy enemy armor punishes low-damage-per-hit kits; beams and pierce restore the math

name: squish index
formula: |{h in picks : pool(h) <= 225}|
rationale: each 225-pool pick is a one-dive target; three of them is a dive invitation

name: weakest-link pool
formula: MIN pool(h) over picks
rationale: focus fire finds the minimum, not the average

name: shield-regen reliance
formula: SUM shield / SUM pool over picks
rationale: shields recharge out of fight: a high share rewards disengage-heavy playstyles and poke maps

name: focus-fire survivability
formula: MIN pool(h) over picks vs MAX single-hit damage stat over enemy kits
rationale: when the enemy's biggest hit exceeds the weakest pool, one mistake is a death, not a retreat

name: weapon-type mix
formula: counts of picks per weapon_configs.weapon_type (hitscan / projectile / beam / arcing)
rationale: all-projectile comps share one weakness; the mix is the comp's damage identity in one line

name: hitscan census
formula: |{h in picks : any weapon_config of h has weapon_type = hitscan}|
rationale: the closest measured proxy for anti-air the schema holds

name: vertical-threat answer
formula: |{h in picks : hitscan}| vs |{e in E : e can fly}|
inputs: flight is not encoded on heroes
rationale: needs a mobility/flight flag on heroes; until then the hitscan census is the honest substitute

name: burst ceiling
formula: MAX single damage stat over the comp's abilities and weapons
rationale: whether the comp can delete a 250hp target through one heal window

name: sustained damage proxy
formula: SUM over picks of MAX damage stat carrying a per-second unit (unit_denominator = second)
rationale: the schema stores per-second figures where the wiki does; summing only those keeps the units honest

name: range profile
formula: MAX range stat per pick; comp median splits poke (>=20m) from brawl (<20m)
rationale: a brawl comp on a poke map loses before the fight starts; range is measured, playstyle is judged - use both

name: beam presence
formula: |{h in picks : any weapon_type = beam}|
rationale: beams ignore travel time and falloff quirks; they are also the armor answer in formula 26

name: close-range dependency
formula: |{h in picks : MAX range stat <= 10}|
rationale: picks that must touch the enemy to contribute all fail together against disengage comps

name: area-damage volume
formula: |{h in picks : any damage stat with a radius stat on the same ability}|
rationale: area damage pressures chokes and barriers without aim; its count is the comp's siege weight

name: one-shot exposure
formula: |{h in picks : pool(h) <= MAX enemy single-hit damage}|
rationale: the mirror of formula 30 from the enemy's seat: how many of ours die to one cooldown

name: enemy coverage
formula: cov(c) = |{e in E : (e, c) in counters}|; report candidates with cov >= COVERAGE_MIN
rationale: one pick answering two named enemies is worth more than two picks answering one each

name: team coverage
formula: |{e in E : exists a in A with (e, a) in counters}| / |E|
rationale: what the locked picks already answer, before spending an open slot on it

name: unanswered-enemy list
formula: {e in E : no a in A answers e}, named explicitly
rationale: the open slots' to-do list, stated as names rather than a percentage

name: net matchup
formula: net(c) = |{e in E : (e,c) in counters}| - |{e in E : (c,e) in counters}|; top NET_LIMIT candidates
rationale: answering two enemies means less if both of them also answer you; the difference is the real edge

name: safe picks
formula: {c in C : no e in E has (c, e) in counters}
rationale: picks the named enemies hold no listed answer to - the low-risk half of the pool

name: exposure count
formula: exp(c) = |{e in E : (c, e) in counters}|, reported inside the net-matchup line
rationale: the denominator of risk: how many named enemies were literally listed as this pick's answer

name: counter diversity
formula: distinct enemies answered by the whole comp / |E|, counting each enemy once
rationale: five picks all answering the same Zarya is 20% breadth wearing a 100% costume

name: coverage redundancy
formula: |{e in E : answered by >= 2 picks}|
rationale: redundant answers survive a swap or a ban; single-threaded answers do not

name: counter-chain instability
formula: |{(c, e) : c answers e but some e' in E answers c}| - answers that are themselves answered
rationale: an answer that dies to the enemy's other half is a swap the enemy can force mid-match

name: ban-resilient coverage
formula: team coverage recomputed with the comp's highest-ban-rate answer removed
rationale: if the plan dies when the likely ban lands, it was never a plan; measure the plan minus its ban

name: proven partners
formula: top PAIRING_LIMIT synergy edges incident to each locked pick, with scores and notes
rationale: the playbook's own memory of what worked next to the pick you already made

name: internal synergy edges
formula: |{(a, b) in synergies : a, b both in picks}| out of C(5,2) = 10 possible
rationale: how much of the comp the playbook has actually seen work together

name: synergy density
formula: internal edges / 10; 0.0 = five strangers, 1.0 = a documented machine
rationale: normalizing lets two candidate comps be compared on cohesion in one number

name: isolated pick
formula: {h in picks : no synergy edge from h to any teammate}
rationale: a great hero with no documented partner in this comp is a solo act - sometimes fine, always worth naming

name: synergy core
formula: largest connected component of the synergy subgraph induced by the picks
rationale: a 4-hero core plus a specialist beats five loosely-paired picks; the component size says which you built

name: score-weighted cohesion
formula: SUM of synergies.score over internal edges (null scores count 0), reported inside the cohesion line
rationale: when the author scored the pairs, the sum ranks comps beyond mere edge count

name: candidate synergy reach
formula: reach(c) = |{a in A : (a, c) in synergies}|
rationale: the direct draft question: which candidate plugs into the picks already locked

name: weak-tie audit
formula: internal edges with score <= WEAK_TIE among the picks
rationale: a low-scored pair the author kept is a documented doubt; surface it rather than average it away

name: synergy hubs
formula: top heroes by degree in the whole synergy graph, restricted to C
rationale: high-degree heroes keep the comp flexible: whatever else changes, they still have partners

name: pairing gravity
formula: rank candidates by (reach(c), mwin(c, map)); synergy first, map rate as tiebreak
rationale: a draft order that respects the playbook's judgement before the population's average

name: map strategy alignment
formula: picks appearing in map_strategy for this map, in the authored rank order
rationale: the playbook's explicit per-map picks; alignment with them is a cited argument, not a vibe

name: style-map intersection
formula: heroes whose playstyle matches the map's top styles AND hold mwin >= 50 on it
rationale: judged style and measured rate agreeing on the same hero is the strongest single signal we compute

name: draft skeleton
formula: greedy fill of the map archetype's role slots from C, allies seated first, ranked by (style match, mwin else win); reports avg win
rationale: a straw-man five to argue against; greedy by design and labeled as such - not an optimum

name: stage volatility
formula: per pick: MAX - MIN of mwin across the map's stages
inputs: map_meta.stage_id exists but holds no rows - the per-stage scrape was cut with the map x tier page budget
rationale: a hero who wins Lighthouse and loses Ruins is a mid-map swap candidate, not a lock - the column is ready; re-widening the rates scrape to stages fills it

name: attack-defense asymmetry
formula: per pick: mwin on attack vs defense for this map
inputs: side is not encoded on map_meta
rationale: the rates page does not split by side; needs a side column and a source that measures it

name: gamemode profile
formula: per pick: mean mwin grouped by maps.gamemode, compared to the current map's mode
rationale: a hero can be a control specialist rather than an Ilios specialist; the mode average separates the two

name: style consensus margin
formula: map_playstyle top score minus second score for this map
rationale: a map judged brawl-by-a-landslide should bind the skeleton harder than a coin-flip map

name: off-map liability
formula: {c : mwin(c, map) <= win(c) - SPECIALIST_DELTA} - the specialist formula's dark twin
rationale: comfort picks that measurably underperform here deserve the same visibility as specialists

name: comp map breadth
formula: |{maps m : mean mwin of picks on m >= 50}| over all maps
rationale: for scrims and tournaments: whether this five is a one-map trick or a portable identity

name: stage specialist
formula: {c : mwin(c, stage) >= mwin(c, map) + SPECIALIST_DELTA for some stage of this map}
inputs: map_meta.stage_id exists but holds no rows - the per-stage scrape was cut with the map x tier page budget
rationale: control maps are three maps in a trenchcoat; a Lighthouse specialist is real information - the column is ready; re-widening the rates scrape to stages fills it

name: sleepers
formula: {c : mwin(c, map) >= SLEEPER_WIN and pick(c) <= SLEEPER_PICK}
rationale: wins a lot, picked rarely: either an inefficiency to exploit or a selection artifact to argue about

name: map specialists
formula: {c : mwin(c, map) >= win(c) + SPECIALIST_DELTA}
rationale: outperforms their own baseline here specifically - the map is doing work for them

name: enemy style lean
formula: modal playstyle among E, when one style holds a strict majority
rationale: naming the enemy's identity (dive, brawl, poke) frames every counter argument that follows

name: ban pressure
formula: flag heroes with ban(h) > 25 as near-certain bans, > 20 as likely
rationale: a comp leaning on a 30%-ban hero needs the plan B written before the ban screen

name: expected availability
formula: PRODUCT over picks of (1 - ban(h)/100): the chance the whole five survives the ban screen
rationale: five 10%-ban picks lose the full comp four matches in ten; the product makes that visible

name: pick-rate mass
formula: SUM pick(h) over picks
rationale: high mass = the mirror-prone meta comp everyone practices against; low mass = off-meta surprise value

name: win-rate trend
formula: delta = win(h) at latest snapshot - win(h) at previous; report |delta| >= TREND_POINTS
rationale: the series the snapshots accumulate exists to be differenced; a 2-point mover is patch news

name: rank sensitivity
formula: per candidate: MAX - MIN win across tiers; flag spreads >= 6 points
rationale: a hero that wins in Bronze and loses in GM is advice that must know its audience

name: population proxy caveat
formula: every rate line inherits queue=RQ, platform=console, region=Americas from its snapshot
rationale: the rates are a proxy for open queue, and the dossier says so every time rather than once

name: over-picked underperformer
formula: {c : pick(c) >= 2 x SLEEPER_PICK and win(c) < 50}
rationale: the sleeper formula's mirror: popularity the results do not justify - do not copy the lobby

name: damage-ult census
formula: |{h in picks : h has an ultimate ability carrying a damage stat}|
rationale: teamfight-ending buttons per fight cycle; zero of them means the comp wins on attrition only

name: ult burst stack
formula: SUM over picks of MAX damage stat on their ultimate
rationale: the ceiling of a coordinated all-in; the number a 'we combo our ults' plan is actually claiming

name: defensive-ult answer
formula: enemy damage ults vs our invulnerability/cleanse ults
inputs: invulnerability is not encoded as a stat
rationale: needs an effect taxonomy (invuln, cleanse, lockout) on abilities; text search is not a formula

name: authored combo notes
formula: synergy edges among picks whose note mentions an ultimate by name
rationale: crude by admission - it reads the author's own words, so it inherits their precision, not the game's

name: ult economy pacing
formula: ult charge cost per hero vs damage/healing throughput
inputs: charge costs are not published or scraped
rationale: Blizzard does not publish charge requirements; without them any pacing number would be fiction

name: cooldown tempo
formula: median cooldown across each pick's abilities; comp median <= 8s reads as high-uptime brawl tempo
rationale: short-cooldown kits re-engage faster; the median is a measured stand-in for 'this comp fights constantly'

name: engage-tool census
formula: |{h in picks : h has a movement ability}|
inputs: movement is not encoded on abilities
rationale: needs an ability-effect taxonomy; until then playstyle 'dive' membership is the judged proxy

name: peel-tool census
formula: |{h in picks : h has a stun/sleep/knockback ability}|
inputs: crowd control is not encoded on abilities
rationale: same missing taxonomy as engage; the counters table encodes its consequences, not the tools

name: objective presence
formula: time-on-objective per hero
inputs: no per-hero objective statistics are scraped
rationale: the rates page publishes win/pick/ban only; this needs a source that does not currently exist in the pipeline

name: swap-cost awareness
formula: ult progress lost per proposed mid-match swap
inputs: live match state is out of scope for the database
rationale: the database describes the game, not a running match; kept to mark the boundary deliberately

name: vintage warning
formula: flag when patches newer than the snapshot's patch exist in patches
rationale: stale rates argue less; the warning explicitly shifts weight toward kit facts and playbook judgement

name: snapshot age
formula: days between captured_at and today, stated on every dossier
rationale: the reader should never have to guess how old the numbers are

name: dual delineation
formula: every snapshot carries both patch_id and season_id, and both predate its capture
rationale: a rate without its patch and season is a number without a 'when'; enforced by invariant test, not convention

name: sample-size caveat
formula: confidence interval on each win rate from its match count
inputs: the rates page publishes no sample sizes
rationale: without n, a 55% is indistinguishable from noise on a rare hero; permanent honesty note until a source appears

name: playbook confidence
formula: per playbook row: an authored confidence grade weighting how hard the dossier leans on it
inputs: no confidence column exists on playbook tables
rationale: today every authored claim argues at equal volume; a confidence column would let the author whisper

name: citation coverage gate
formula: every recorded pick must cite >= 1 evidence tag that the dossier actually rendered
rationale: enforced at write time: an answer that cites nothing, or cites the unseen, is refused, not warned

name: history echo
formula: prior recorded recommendations for the same map, surfaced as evidence
rationale: the system's own past answers are data; agreeing or breaking with them should be a conscious act

name: skeleton dissent
formula: picks in the recorded answer that differ from the draft skeleton, counted and named
inputs: recommendation_picks vs the skeleton at record time
rationale: divergence from the greedy baseline is where the model earned its keep - or went wrong; either way, log it

name: catalog parity
formula: set of derived: tags emitted by dossier.py = set of tags on live derived rows in this table
rationale: self-referential integrity, enforced by test: the catalog may never drift from the code it describes

name: the objective
formula: COUNTER = argmax over 5-subsets of C of w1*coverage + w2*cohesion + w3*map fit + w4*meta - w5*exposure
inputs: every table above; weights would live in heuristic_params
rationale: the whole database in one line; the skeleton greedily approximates it, and an exact solver is the roadmap
